meta.title: Hooft & Petiet and ReShare, the plan
meta.desc: The plan around the two new sites for Hooft & Petiet and ReShare Living Group, every figure sourced, prepared by Astra in October 2026.

cover.h: Hooft & Petiet and ReShare, the plan.
cover.lede: Willem asked us to send this to your team. Two sites are built, one for each brand, and this is the plan around them. It's written for two things, more renovation projects for Hooft & Petiet, and a home for the circular story ReShare was set up to tell.

market.h: The work runs to 2034 at least.
market.lede: Corporations tackle nearly 90,000 homes a year. They agreed to improve every home with an E, F or G label by the end of 2028, and the average heat demand of their homes has to fall from 108 kWh per m² to under 94 by 2030 and under 87 by the end of 2034. In every project somebody decides whether residents stay home, rest somewhere quiet in the day, or move out for weeks. That’s the decision the Hooft & Petiet site has to win.

items.h: The Hoge Raad on furnished swap homes
items.p: A tenant offered a fully furnished and fitted swap home is in principle not owed the minimum moving allowance.

items.h: Heat demand under 94, and half the raw materials
items.p: The national aim is half the primary raw materials by 2030, and PBL calls that very unlikely on current trends. KeyPro words the purchasing aim as 50% circular by 2030.
The next ceiling in the national agreements.
The Dutch goal ReShare is built for.

allowance.h: A furnished home is also a legal answer.
allowance.lede: Tenants who have to leave for a renovation are owed a minimum moving allowance, €7,926 for moves since 28 February 2026. On 1 April 2022 the Hoge Raad ruled that a tenant offered a fully furnished and fitted swap home is in principle not entitled to that minimum, also when they turn a reasonable offer down. Location and quality, the length of the stay, whether belongings have to move and the tenant’s circumstances decide whether the offer is reasonable, and costs like transport and storage remain. That belongs on the Hooft & Petiet site, in plain words, checked by a lawyer, right next to the request.
allowance.calc_note: The statutory minimum per household times the number you enter. Whether it's owed depends on the offer, as the ruling says. It isn't a saving we promise.
allowance.src: Rijksoverheid, “Wanneer heb ik recht op verhuiskostenvergoeding?”, read 25 Oct 2026. Dirkzwager, Robert Rijpstra and Lotte Blum, on ECLI:NL:HR:2022:493, 7 Apr 2022.

rivals.h: Two rivals already show proof on the first screen.
rivals.lede: We read the homepages of the firms a project leader finds next to you. Moving-In shows Portaal and Havensteder, two names from your own logo row, and a 9.4 out of 10 from Feedback Company in its header. Furniture Lease shows named reviews and a package from €149.50. You have an independent 8 to 8.5 from residents, and it sits in a news post from 2020.

position.h: “Alleen de koffer moet nog door de bewoners worden uitgepakt.”
position.lede: Only the suitcase is left for the residents to unpack. It’s Brenda de Wilde’s line, and the new site is built to prove it. Rows that show what you take off a corporation’s hands, projects told by the people involved, the residents’ score next to the request, and the group behind it on the ReShare site.
position.src: Brenda de Wilde, project manager at Hooft & Petiet, on the Cazas Wonen article, read 25 Oct 2026.

hubspot.lede: Your current site already loads HubSpot. When the new site goes live, the availability bar and the quote form send their answers there as a deal, the kind of home, how many, the start month and how long, so whoever picks it up can answer with dates. Each request carries the page it came from, which is how you’ll see which pages win projects.
